docs.title: Cursor Agent Skills
docs.text:
This site is the canonical documentation for agent skills published from the docs/ tree: catalog pages, per-skill reference, recipes, and a short cookbook.

In Cursor, @mention a skill so the agent loads the project’s SKILL.md implementation (often colocated with this repo under skills/<name>/ or skills-cursor/<name>/).

docs.title: What you will find
docs.text: Section Purpose Getting started Invoke skills, @mention patterns, workflow diagram Skills → Catalog Grouped index + links to one page per skill Recipe: calendar refresh Long-form, copy-paste multi-thread flow Cookbook Short prompts (API slice, triage, Neon, PR, etc.)

docs.title: Deployed docs
docs.text: Built with MkDocs and Material. Pushes to main that touch docs/ or .github/workflows/docs.yml deploy to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Local preview
docs.text:
cd docs
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

Open the URL shown in the terminal (often http://127.0.0.1:8000).

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Skills are markdown instructions the agent reads when your task matches their description. They keep behavior consistent: when to align, when to test, when to file issues, and what not to do.

docs.title: Where skills live
docs.text:
• In Cursor: .cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, skills/<name>/, or paths you configure.
  • On this site: Browse the Skills catalog—each skill has its own page under Skills in the sidebar.

docs.title: How to invoke a skill
docs.text:
Use an @mention in chat so the agent loads the right skill before writing code or tests.

Minimal pattern

@tdd — Public API: createCheckout(cart). First behavior: happy path succeeds.

The agent should confirm the behavior list, then write one failing test, then minimal code.

docs.title: Choose a workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR A[New idea / PRD] --> B{Artifact?} B -->|Local plan| C[prd-to-plan] B -->|GitHub issues| D[prd-to-issues] A --> E[grill-me] F[Unfamiliar repo] --> G[inherited-codebase-onboarding] H[Bug] --> I[triage-issue] J[Implement slice] --> K[aligned-implementation + tdd]
  • Product clarity: grill-me, prd-critique
  • Plan or tickets: prd-to-plan, prd-to-issues
  • Orientation: inherited-codebase-onboarding
  • Shipping a slice: aligned-implementation + tdd
  • GitHub: issue-to-pr after your branch is ready

docs.title: Rules that work well
docs.text:
1. One anchor per thread — issue number, plan section, or pasted scope block; avoid mixing unrelated features.
  2. Approve before RED — for aligned-implementation and tdd, settle the public API and “done for this thread” before the first failing test.
  3. Vertical slices — each PR or thread should deliver something end-to-end and demoable, not “all models then all controllers.”
  4. Escalate with the right skill — tangled code → improve-codebase-architecture or request-refactor-plan; Neon egress → neon-postgres-egress-optimizer.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Open the Skills catalog and jump to the pages you reuse most.
  • Walk the calendar refresh recipe to see skills in sequence.
  • Copy from Cookbook: quick examples.

docs.title: Cookbook: quick examples
docs.text: Short, copy-paste patterns with real wording. Replace bracketed placeholders with your project facts.

docs.title: 1. Scoped API slice (auth + validation)
docs.text:
Goal: Add one endpoint with alignment and tests—no drive-by refactors.

Prompt

@aligned-implementation @tdd

Anchor: issue #88 — POST /api/v1/invites.

Phase 0 — align now:
- Request body: { email, role } — role enum: admin | member.
- Behaviors in order: (1) 201 + invite id when email new, (2) 409 when duplicate invite, (3) 400 when role invalid.
- Done for this thread: handler + tests for this route only; no email sending implementation (stub port).

Stop for my OK before RED. Then one failing test → minimal green → repeat.

Why it works: The anchor is one issue, behaviors are ordered, and out-of-scope work (real email) is explicitly stubbed.

docs.title: 2. Bug triage with a TDD fix plan
docs.text:
Goal: Root cause + GitHub issue with RED/GREEN steps—implementation optional in a follow-up.

Prompt

@triage-issue

Symptom: Invoice PDF shows wrong tax when a line item has a discount; total matches but line tax does not.

Reproduce: Add item $100, 10% discount, tax 8%; export PDF — line tax column ignores discount.

Investigate, file a GitHub issue with RCA and a TDD plan. Do not implement the fix in this thread unless I ask.

Pairs with: @tdd + @aligned-implementation on a branch named from the new issue.

docs.title: 3. Neon: high egress from list endpoints
docs.text:
Goal: Map hot queries to application code and reduce bytes returned.

Prompt

@neon-postgres-egress-optimizer

Symptom: Neon transfer/egress jumped after shipping dashboard v2. We use pg_stat_statements.

Find top queries by rows returned; map to ORM/repo calls. Recommend: column lists, pagination, split JOINs, or cache for hot static reads. Prioritize by impact.

Pairs with: @neon-postgres for connection and platform details.

docs.title: 4. PRD → phased plan on disk
docs.text:
Goal: Local ./plans/feature.md with vertical phases—not a pile of horizontal tasks.

Prompt

@prd-to-plan

PRD path: ./prd.md (notifications reliability).

Explore the repo only enough to name real integration points: DB, queue, mobile push, email provider.

Output: ./plans/notifications-reliability.md with:
- Cross-cutting decisions (idempotency, dedupe key, timezone).
- Phases as vertical slices (each phase demoable end-to-end).

Quiz me on granularity; write the file after I approve the outline.

docs.title: 5. Issue → branch → PR (automation)
docs.text:
Goal: Branch from latest main, commit with message you approve, open PR via gh.

Prompt

@issue-to-pr — #42, base main. Use conventional commits. Draft PR; I’ll approve commit and PR bodies before you push.

Requires: gh authenticated, origin writable, clean or agreed scope for staged files.

docs.title: Combining skills (cheat sheet)
docs.text:
Intent Skills Narrow scope + test-first aligned-implementation + tdd Sharpen PRD before planning prd-critique → prd-to-plan GitHub issues instead of local plan prd-to-issues Repo map + next step inherited-codebase-onboarding Architecture RFC improve-codebase-architecture or request-refactor-plan Mid-flight scope change requirement-course-correction

See the Skills catalog and each skill’s page for combinations and quickstarts.

docs.title: Recipe: calendar refresh (end-to-end flow)
docs.text:
Scenario: Calendar works but feels dated; creating events is slow; repeats are limited (week / month / bi-week, max 10 instances); notifications are unreliable; visual design must stay strong—you want smoother behavior without a visual rewrite.

Use this as a sequence of chat threads (or one long thread if you keep context). Each block is copy-paste ready and names the skill so the agent follows it.

docs.title: 0. Problem anchor (paste once at the top of thread 1)
docs.text:
Context (do not rewrite—use as scope anchor):
- App has a calendar feature: looks good, interaction model is slow/clunky.
- Creating events takes too many steps / too long.
- Recurring events: only week, month, bi-week; max 10 instances.
- Notifications exist but behave unreliably (“ropey”).
- Non-negotiable: preserve current visual quality; improve flow and reliability.

docs.title: 1. Formalise the issue — grill-me
docs.text:
Goal: Close decisions that a plan will depend on (recurrence model, caps, notification guarantees, what “seamless” means in measurable terms).

Copy-paste:

@grill-me

Context: [paste block from §0]

Grill me until we have explicit decisions for:
1) Primary user job for v1 (e.g. “create a one-off event fast” vs “manage recurring series”).
2) Recurrence: keep weekly/monthly/biweekly only, or expand (daily, custom RRULE, “forever” series)? Max instances vs end date?
3) Notifications: which channels (in-app, email, push), what “reliable” means (delivery SLA, dedupe, timezone), known failure modes.
4) What must not change visually (screens/components frozen) vs what can move (layout micro-tweaks for fewer steps).

One focused question at a time; after each answer, give your recommended default and short rationale.

Optional next thread — ubiquitous-language (only if “event / series / instance / reminder” get mixed):

@ubiquitous-language

We’re standardising terms for calendar work. From this thread and prior answers, write UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md: Event vs Series vs Occurrence vs Reminder; what we call the 10-instance cap; notification vs alert.

Written anchor (pick one):

  • Lightweight: open GitHub issue “Calendar: UX + recurrence + notifications” with §0 + answers from grill-me; note issue number as #CAL for later.
  • Heavier: add ./prd.md from those answers → @prd-critique → ./plans/prd-final.md.

docs.title: 2. Interrogate the code — inherited-codebase-onboarding
docs.text:
Goal: Map routes/screens, data layer, recurrence storage, notification pipeline, tests—no refactors.

Copy-paste:

@inherited-codebase-onboarding

Bounded reconnaissance only—no refactors.

Scope: calendar feature and anything that creates/edits events, stores recurrence (week/month/biweek, 10-instance cap), and sends or schedules notifications.

Deliver:
1) Entry points (routes, screens, jobs/cron).
2) Where recurrence rules and instance limits are enforced (client vs server).
3) Notification path (queue, provider, idempotency, retries)—where it can flake.
4) Test coverage map for the above.
5) Numbered list of follow-ups; I’ll reply with one number for the next thread.

Assume visual design files exist and are off-limits unless I say otherwise.

If onboarding surfaces a specific bug (“notifications lost on retry”): new thread triage-issue:

@triage-issue

Symptom: [one sentence, e.g. duplicate reminders / missed push / wrong timezone].

Reproduce: [steps]. Investigate root cause and file a GitHub issue with a TDD fix plan (RED/GREEN). Do not implement in this thread unless I ask.

If onboarding shows tangled modules and you can’t slice features safely: new thread improve-codebase-architecture:

@improve-codebase-architecture

From onboarding, the worst coupling is: [calendar + notifications / recurrence + DB / …]. Explore and propose numbered deep-module candidates; I’ll pick one for an RFC issue. No implementation.

docs.title: Option A — Markdown plan — prd-to-plan
docs.text:
Prereq: PRD or summary in chat (paste §0 + grill-me decisions + 5 bullets from onboarding).

Copy-paste:

@prd-to-plan

PRD/summary is below. Explore the repo only enough to name real integration layers (API, DB, jobs, UI)—not file-level refactors.

Summary:
[paste §0]
Decisions from grill-me:
[paste bullets]
Onboarding highlights:
[paste 3–5 bullets: where calendar lives, recurrence enforced, notification path]

Produce ./plans/calendar-refresh.md with:
- Architectural decisions that apply to all phases (auth, timezone storage, notification channel).
- Phases as vertical slices only (each phase demoable end-to-end).

Proposed phase themes (adjust after exploration):
1) Fast path: create a **single** non-recurring event with fewer steps (keep current look).
2) Recurrence: new rules and/or limits **as decided in grill-me** (replace 10-cap story if we’re changing product rules).
3) Notifications: one reliability slice (e.g. schedule + dedupe + test)—channel chosen in grill-me.

Quiz me on granularity; then write the file after I approve.

docs.title: Option B — GitHub issues — prd-to-issues
docs.text:
Prereq: Parent issue exists (e.g. epic #100 with §0 + decisions).

Copy-paste:

@prd-to-issues

Parent PRD/epic is issue #100 (calendar UX + recurrence + notifications). Break into vertical-slice child issues: prefer AFK; mark HITL only for product/security decisions. Show numbered breakdown with blockers; do not create until I approve; then create in dependency order.

docs.title: Option C — Refactor-first RFC — request-refactor-plan
docs.text:
Use when the main risk is code structure, not missing product clarity.

@request-refactor-plan

Problem: calendar + notification code is tangled; we need a safe seam before feature slices.

Interview me, then file a GitHub issue: problem, solution, micro-commit plan, testing decisions, out of scope. No implementation in this thread.

docs.title: 4. Implement — tracer bullets — aligned-implementation + tdd
docs.text: Rule: One thread per vertical slice (or one slice per PR). Each thread has one anchor: ./plans/calendar-refresh.md section or issue number.

docs.title: Slice example A — fast single-event create
docs.text:
@aligned-implementation @tdd

Anchor: ./plans/calendar-refresh.md — Phase 1 (fast single-event create). GitHub issue #101 if applicable.

Phase 0 — align now:
- Public surface: [e.g. create-event modal flow / API route—fill from onboarding]
- Behaviours to prove in order: (1) default duration/title valid submit, (2) cancel preserves calendar state, (3) error shown on invalid time
- Done for this thread: Phase 1 acceptance criteria checked for the single-event path only; **no** recurrence changes.

Stop for my explicit OK before RED.

Then: one failing test → minimal green → repeat. Refactor only when green.

docs.title: Slice example B — recurrence product change
docs.text:
@aligned-implementation @tdd

Anchor: ./plans/calendar-refresh.md — Phase 2 (recurrence). Issue #102.

Phase 0:
- Recurrence rules we agreed in grill-me: [paste]
- Backward compatibility: existing series with 10-cap must [migrate / display legacy / …]

One behaviour per cycle; first test is smallest end-to-end proof (e.g. create biweekly series with new cap rule). Approve scope before RED.

docs.title: Slice example C — notifications reliability
docs.text:
@aligned-implementation @tdd

Anchor: ./plans/calendar-refresh.md — Phase 3 (notifications). Issue #103.

Phase 0:
- Observable behaviour: [e.g. exactly one reminder per occurrence; idempotent schedule job]
- Out of scope: [e.g. new push provider]

First failing test should assert **user-visible or API-visible** outcome, not internal queue details unless that’s the only seam.

docs.title: When scope shifts mid-flight — requirement-course-correction
docs.text:
@requirement-course-correction

Change: [e.g. “legal wants audit log on notification sends”]. Plan: ./plans/calendar-refresh.md. Parent issue #100.

Classify (bug vs spec vs requirement vs architecture), run impact checklist, propose plan/issue edits, stop for my “Approved: implement only [X]” before code.

docs.title: Order summary (calendar-shaped project)
docs.text:
Order Skill Calendar-specific output 1 grill-me Decisions on speed vs recurrence vs notifications; visual freeze 2 ubiquitous-language Optional glossary 3 inherited-codebase-onboarding Map + numbered next steps 3b triage-issue or improve-codebase-architecture Only if bug or coupling blocks slices 4 prd-to-plan or prd-to-issues ./plans/calendar-refresh.md or child issues 5 aligned-implementation + tdd One thread per phase (fast create → recurrence → notifications) — requirement-course-correction When requirements move mid-project

This is a usage flow: skills do not chain automatically—you open each thread with the right @ and paste the anchor text so behaviour matches the skill you invoked.

docs.title: aligned-implementation
docs.text: Skill package: aligned-implementation/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Keeps implementation work narrow, test-first in vertical slices, and aligned with you before scope grows.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: A scope anchor (issue number/URL, path to markdown spec/plan, or pasted brief). If none: the agent proposes a short in/out/done paragraph and waits for approval. Your confirmation on public surface, prioritized behaviors, and “done” for this thread.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Phased work: align → one failing “tracer” test → minimal code → repeat; optional bounded architecture discussion; refactor only when green. Optional per-cycle checklist text you can paste.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace deep TDD or architecture skills; it orchestrates. Not for one-line fixes, pure explanation, or huge upfront design with no code when you asked for that.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: @mention the skill. Do not let the agent write tests or code until Phase 0 is settled. Insist on one test → one behavior → minimal pass. Block “while we’re here” refactors and new docs unless you asked.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Issue #42 + ./plans/auth.md section 2 — implement password reset slice only; align on API shape first.”
  2. “No issue — here’s scope: [paste]. Approve before RED.”
  3. After first green: “Next behavior only: expired token returns 401.”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• tdd — mechanics of red-green-refactor.
  • prd-to-plan or prd-to-issues — anchors for scope.
  • improve-codebase-architecture — only for Phase 3 when coupling blocks the slice.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @aligned-implementation — Anchor: issue #42. Phase 0: public API is POST /reset with email + token; done = one happy path + one invalid token. Approve before tests.

docs.title: create-rule
docs.text: Skill package: skills-cursor/create-rule/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Creates Cursor project rules as .mdc files under .cursor/rules/ with YAML frontmatter for scope and globs.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Purpose; always vs file-scoped; glob patterns (e.g. **/*.ts) if scoped; can infer from conversation.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One focused .mdc per rule (under ~50 lines recommended); description, globs, alwaysApply as needed; examples inside.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace skills for long workflows; put rules in skills-cursor (that’s Cursor’s internal space).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Answer scope vs always-apply; give precise globs; keep one concern per file.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Always: error handling pattern for TS.”
  2. globs: **/*.tsx — React conventions.
  3. Split when a rule exceeds one concern.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• create-skill — heavier workflows.
  • migrate-to-skills — convert old rules to skills.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @create-rule — Enforce: no empty catch blocks in TypeScript. Scope: **/*.ts only. Add description + example.

docs.title: create-skill
docs.text: Skill package: skills-cursor/create-skill/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Guides creation of Agent Skills: skill-name/SKILL.md, frontmatter, optional reference.md, examples.md, scripts/.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Purpose, personal vs project path, triggers, domain facts, output format; not in ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Valid name + description (third person, WHAT+WHEN); concise body (<500 lines); progressive disclosure pattern.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Teach the agent everything it already knows—stay token-efficient.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Follow discovery → design → implementation → verification; link references one level deep.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Team PR review skill with checklist.
  2. PDF skill with scripts/extract.py.
  3. Description: “Processes X. Use when user mentions Y or Z.”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• create-rule — lighter persistence.
  • migrate-to-skills — from .mdc rules.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @create-skill — Skill: generate release notes from merged PRs. Project: .cursor/skills/. Triggers: release, changelog, ship.

docs.title: create-subagent
docs.text: Skill package: skills-cursor/create-subagent/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Defines custom subagents as .md in .cursor/agents/ or ~/.cursor/agents/ with YAML frontmatter + system prompt body.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name, description (when to delegate), focused behavior; project vs user scope.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: name.md with name + description; body = instructions for the subagent; the skill file itself may use disable-model-invocation separately from subagent files.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace Skills—subagents are delegated workers with isolated context.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Pick scope; write detailed description with trigger terms; test with “Use subagent X to …”.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. code-reviewer.md — post-change review.
  2. debugger.md — RCA workflow.
  3. Project agents in repo for team sharing.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text: • design-an-interface / improve-codebase-architecture — use Task/subagents for parallel designs; custom subagents for repeated roles.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @create-subagent — Project agent: API contract reviewer. Invoked after OpenAPI changes. Put in .cursor/agents/.

docs.title: design-an-interface
docs.text: Skill package: design-an-interface/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Produces several radically different interface designs for a module (via parallel sub-agents), then compares trade-offs in prose.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Module purpose, callers, key operations, constraints, what to hide vs expose. Optionally “design it twice” or parallel exploration.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Per design: signature, usage example, what it hides, trade-offs; then prose comparison (simplicity, flexibility, efficiency, depth, misuse risk). No implementation.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Ship code; substitute for your final product decision; guarantee “best” without your choice.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Ask for requirements first. Have the agent spawn 3+ Task sub-agents in one message with different constraints each (e.g. minimal API vs maximal flexibility vs common case). Read designs sequentially, then comparison.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Payment adapter: three designs — minimal methods, plugin-style, and optimized for card-only.”
  2. “Job queue client: contrast callback vs polling vs stream.”
  3. “After comparison, blend A’s surface with B’s error model.”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• improve-codebase-architecture — explores coupling first; this skill narrows API shape.
  • aligned-implementation + tdd — implement after you pick a design.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @design-an-interface — Module: email outbox. Callers: order service + workers. Generate 3+ different shapes; compare depth and caller misuse risk. No code.

docs.title: greenfield-scaffold
docs.text: Skill package: greenfield-scaffold/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Scaffolds a new repo’s Phase 0: pins, format/lint, tests, CI, minimal entry point—before feature work.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Approved PRD/plan or explicit spike waiver; ./plans/<slug>.md with Phase 0 acceptance criteria; empty folder or skeleton.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Repo with version pins, test / lint / format commands, CI on PR, minimal CLI --help or health check, short install/run notes; checkboxes aligned to plan.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace your feature design; build Phase 1+ unless you ask.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Ensure Phase 0 is written in the plan. Invoke with @mentions; say “Phase 0 only” if you want no features.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Phase 0 per ./plans/saas.md — Node 22, eslint, vitest, GHA on PR.”
  2. “CLI only: mytool --help exits 0.”
  3. “After green CI, stop — no Phase 1.”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• prd-to-plan — produces phased plan.
  • aligned-implementation + tdd — tests for Phase 0 smoke.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @greenfield-scaffold @aligned-implementation @tdd — Phase 0 only per ./plans/widget.md. Parent issue #5. Do not start Phase 1.

docs.title: grill-me
docs.text: Skill package: grill-me/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Interviews you until the plan or design is explicit enough that tradeoffs and dependencies are clear.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: A plan, design, or decision to stress-test; optional repo context.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One focused question at a time (or a tight cluster), each with a recommended answer and rationale; branches closed with agreed decision or deferral; codebase facts when discoverable.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace implementation; stay hostile; ask endless questions without using the repo when answers are there.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Say “grill me on [topic].” Answer precisely; override recommendations when needed. Expect hidden assumptions, constraints, and contract clarity (errors, idempotency).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Grill me on the caching plan for exports.”
  2. “Before more questions, read the export pipeline and then ask about idempotency.”
  3. Close branch: “We agree Redis + 5m TTL; owner = platform team.”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• prd-critique — hardens product docs.
  • request-refactor-plan — turns grilled decisions into an RFC issue.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @grill-me — Plan: migrate auth to OAuth2. Resolve decision tree: tenants, rollback, session invalidation. One question at a time.

docs.title: improve-codebase-architecture
docs.text: Skill package: improve-codebase-architecture/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Explores the codebase for friction, proposes deep-module opportunities, runs parallel interface designs for a chosen cluster, and files a GitHub refactor RFC issue (no prior approval step for creating the issue).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Repo access; your interest in architecture, testability, or AI-navigability. You pick one candidate from the numbered list.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Numbered candidate clusters (coupling, dependency category, test impact); user-facing problem framing; 3+ parallel interface designs; recommendation; gh issue create URL with RFC template.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Guarantee implementation; skip exploration—organic friction is the signal.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Let the agent explore with Explore sub-agents. Review candidates; pick one. Read the problem-space framing before design sub-agents return. Expect an issue URL at the end.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Find shallow modules in billing/.”
  2. “Candidate 2 — deepen the invoice boundary; file RFC.”
  3. Use the issue as a backlog item for a future PR.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• inherited-codebase-onboarding — orientation first.
  • design-an-interface — similar parallel designs but this skill ties to clusters and RFC filing.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @improve-codebase-architecture — Bounded pass on `src/payments/`. Number candidates; I’ll pick one for deep-module RFC.

docs.title: inherited-codebase-onboarding

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Bounded reconnaissance: docs, entry points, tests, data boundaries, risk flags—no refactors.

docs.title: Input

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Short summary plus numbered follow-ups; you reply with one number or “feature X instead.”

docs.title: What it won’t do

docs.title: How to use it

docs.title: Examples

  2. “Reply 3 to dig into coupling next.”
  3. Combine with architecture skill for numbered clusters.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• improve-codebase-architecture — next step.
  • triage-issue — bugs before speculative refactors.

docs.title: issue-to-pr
docs.text: Skill package: issue-to-pr/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Creates branch issue-<N>-<slug> from origin/<base>, drafts commit/PR text from gh issue view, gets approval (AskQuestion), commits, pushes, opens PR with gh—same repo, direct push to origin.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Issue number (#42 or issue 42); optional base branch (default main); optional --draft or conventional prefix.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Branch, commit, PR URL; duplicate PR detection if head already has open PR.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Fork workflows; commit without approval; git add -A without agreement; silently drop local work.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Ensure gh auth and origin. Name paths or use git add -p when staging. Approve exact commit + PR bodies when prompted.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Issue-to-PR for #42 into main.”
  2. “#128, base develop, draft PR.”
  3. Stash first if you have dirty tree on another branch.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• mirror-repo-github — ensures writable origin on GitHub.
  • Works after any feature work following aligned-implementation.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @issue-to-pr — #42, base main. Conventional commits. Draft PR after I approve messages.

docs.title: migrate-to-skills
docs.text: Skill package: skills-cursor/migrate-to-skills/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Migrates “Applied intelligently” .cursor/rules/*.mdc (no globs, not alwaysApply) and slash commands .cursor/commands/*.md to .cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, verbatim body.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Project or user ~/.cursor/commands; rules matching migration criteria; Task sub-agents when available for parallel work.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: New SKILL.md files; originals deleted; summary list; undo instructions if asked.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Migrate alwaysApply or globs rules (those stay rules); modify body content (forbidden).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Back up or commit first; run migration; verify skills; ask agent to undo by restoring originals if needed.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Intelligent” rules → skills for model discovery.
  2. /commit command → skill with disable-model-invocation: true.
  3. Team adopts skills directory convention.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• create-skill — author new skills after migration.
  • create-rule — what stays as rules.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @migrate-to-skills — Migrate eligible project rules and commands under .cursor/ to .cursor/skills/. Preserve bodies exactly.

docs.title: mirror-repo-github
docs.text: Skill package: mirror-repo-github/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Removes old origin, creates a new private GitHub repo with gh, wires origin, pushes—so automation (e.g. issue-to-pr) has a home.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Target owner/repo (or repo name + gh user as owner); branch to push (default rules around main/master); never public unless you change outside this skill.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: origin → new URL; branch pushed; optional verification.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Create public repos in this workflow; force-push without explicit ask; remove other remotes unless you ask.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: gh auth login; run from repo root. Prefer gh repo create owner/name --private --source=. --remote=origin --push when suitable.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Mirror this clone to acme/widget-api private.”
  2. “Detach old origin; I need a fresh repo for gh workflows.”
  3. Large history: expect push to take time.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text: • issue-to-pr — needs origin you control.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @mirror-repo-github — New private repo `myuser/experiment`. Push current branch.

docs.title: neon-postgres-egress-optimizer
docs.text: Skill package: neon-postgres-egress-optimizer/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Diagnoses and fixes application-side patterns that inflate Postgres egress (bytes returned to the app).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Symptoms (high bill, spikes, SELECT *, N+1); optional pg_stat_statements access; or codebase-only review.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Ranked findings; fixes: column lists, pagination, caching hot static reads, SQL-side aggregation, splitting JOINs to avoid duplication; verification steps.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace Neon pricing support; fix non-egress issues (pure CPU) unless they correlate; guarantee stats if compute just restarted (stats may be empty).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Enable/reset pg_stat_statements if needed; run diagnostic queries; map top queries to code; apply fixes; reset stats and re-measure.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Top queries by rows — this endpoint selects all columns.”
  2. “Split product+reviews JOIN into two queries.”
  3. “Cache reference data queried 50k times/day.”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• neon-postgres — platform context.
  • Neon billing docs for transfer semantics.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @neon-postgres-egress-optimizer — Bill spiked; we have pg_stat_statements. Find top row-returning queries and map to ORM calls.

docs.title: neon-postgres

docs.title: What it does

docs.title: Output

docs.title: What it won’t do

docs.title: How to use it

docs.title: Examples

1. “Pooled vs direct host for serverless?”
  2. “Branch for preview deploys?”
  3. “Neon Auth vs Neon JS for my Next app?”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• neon-postgres-egress-optimizer — cost/transfer.
  • MCP Neon tools in Cursor — live SQL/projects when configured.

docs.title: prd-critique
docs.text: Skill package: prd-critique/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Reviews ./prd.md like a tough PM, then writes ./plans/prd-final.md with Stripe-style structure plus embedded PRD Review Notes (critique).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: ./prd.md required; optional spec.md, notes.md, research.md, context.md.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Single markdown file: title, review notes (missing/ambiguous/over-specified/contradictions/questions), then Final PRD in fixed section order.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace a technical spec; succeed if prd.md is missing (fail clearly); invent business facts without context.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Put draft at ./prd.md; optional supporting files; run skill; read prd-final.md for decisions and remaining open questions.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Draft PRD → critique → sharper v1 scope.
  2. Thin PRD → review notes call it out + best-effort final with assumptions.
  3. Spec-heavy draft → extract product layer into PRD.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• prd-to-plan — turns final PRD into phases.
  • prd-to-issues — if PRD lives as GitHub issue.
  • grill-me — live Q&A instead of file-based critique.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @prd-critique — ./prd.md is ready. Produce ./plans/prd-final.md with review notes + Stripe-style final PRD.

docs.title: prd-to-issues
docs.text: Skill package: prd-to-issues/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Breaks a PRD into vertical-slice GitHub issues (tracer bullets), quizzes you, then gh issue create per slice in dependency order.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: PRD GitHub issue number or URL; optional codebase exploration; your approval on breakdown.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Numbered proposal (title, HITL/AFK, blocked by, user stories); then created issues with parent link, acceptance criteria, blockers.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Close or edit the parent PRD issue; horizontal “all DB then all API” tickets.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Provide PRD issue #; iterate on granularity; confirm HITL vs AFK; let agent create issues blockers-first.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “PRD #100 — slice into AFK issues where possible.”
  2. “Merge slices 2 and 3 — too thin.”
  3. Track work from issue board.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• prd-to-plan — local phased plan vs GitHub issues.
  • aligned-implementation — implement one issue per thread.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @prd-to-issues — Parent PRD is issue #100. Vertical slices only; prefer AFK; show breakdown before creating issues.

docs.title: prd-to-plan
docs.text: Skill package: prd-to-plan/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Turns a PRD into a multi-phase tracer-bullet plan saved as ./plans/<feature>.md.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: PRD in chat or path; optional codebase exploration; durable decisions (routes, schema shape, auth).

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Markdown plan: architectural decisions, then phases with “What to build” + acceptance criteria; no brittle file/function names.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Create GitHub issues (use prd-to-issues); skip your approval on breakdown.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Paste or point to PRD; answer granularity quiz; use Phase 0 with greenfield-scaffold when starting from scratch.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Plan for onboarding PRD → ./plans/user-onboarding.md.”
  2. “Split phase 2 — too big.”
  3. Phases become sprint boundaries.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• greenfield-scaffold — Phase 0.
  • prd-to-issues — alternative artifact.
  • prd-critique — sharpen PRD first.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @prd-to-plan — PRD is in ./prd.md. Explore repo briefly; propose vertical phases; write ./plans/onboarding.md after I approve.

docs.title: request-refactor-plan
docs.text: Skill package: request-refactor-plan/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Interviews you, explores the repo, alternatives, scope, tests; splits work into tiny commits; creates a GitHub issue with the refactor template.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Long description of problem and ideas; willingness to answer detailed questions.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: gh issue create with: problem, solution, commits list, decisions, testing decisions, out of scope—no file paths/snippets in the issue per skill.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Skip the interview; guarantee the refactor is executed in the same session.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Come prepared with problem statement; engage on alternatives and test strategy; use issue as execution guide.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Extract payment adapter; plan micro-commits.”
  2. “Insufficient tests — agent asks your plan.”
  3. Issue becomes team RFC.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• improve-codebase-architecture — RFC from exploration.
  • tdd — execute plan in slices.
  • requirement-course-correction — architecture debt path.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @request-refactor-plan — Problem: god module in billing. Goal: seam for providers. I want tiny commits and a gh issue at the end.

docs.title: requirement-course-correction
docs.text: Skill package: requirement-course-correction/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Classifies mid-flight change (bug vs spec vs requirement vs architecture), updates plan/issues, gets Approved for one slice, implements one vertical slice with aligned-implementation + tdd.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Summary of change; ./plans/<slug>.md; parent issue #; explicit “Approved” for what to implement.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Classification + impact checklist updates; one implemented slice anchored to updated issue/plan.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Large refactor without request-refactor-plan; silent scope creep.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: @mention with change summary; review classification; approve single anchor; one slice per thread.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Business rule changed — update PRD phases 3–4 and issue #12.”
  2. “Bug vs spec: use triage-issue for bug.”
  3. “Approved: implement only subsection 2.1.”

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text: Use with triage-issue (bugs), request-refactor-plan (big refactors), prd-to-plan (plan updates), aligned-implementation, and tdd—pick by change class.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @requirement-course-correction — Requirement change: [summary]. Plan: ./plans/app.md. Parent #N. Classify, propose edits, stop for Approved before code.

docs.title: tdd
docs.text: Skill package: tdd/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Teaches red-green-refactor with vertical slices (tracer bullets), behavior through public interfaces, and anti-patterns.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Feature or bug fix with agreed interface and prioritized behaviors; your approval on plan before code.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One failing test → minimal pass → repeat; refactor only when green; pointers to bundled tests.md, mocking.md, etc.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Endorse “write all tests then all code” (horizontal slice); test everything exhaustively without prioritization.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Confirm public API and behaviors; one test at a time; refuse refactors while RED.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. First test: “valid cart checks out.”
  2. Next: “empty cart rejected.”
  3. Green: extract duplication.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• aligned-implementation — process gates.
  • triage-issue — TDD fix plan in issue body.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
@tdd @aligned-implementation — Public API: `checkout(cart)`. Behaviors: happy path, empty cart, expired offer. One test at a time.

docs.title: triage-issue
docs.text: Skill package: triage-issue/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Explores the codebase for root cause, then creates a GitHub issue with problem, RCA, and TDD fix plan (RED/GREEN cycles)—minimal user questions.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Brief problem description (or one question to get it).

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Issue URL; RCA in behavior/contract terms (not fragile layout); numbered RED/GREEN cycles + optional REFACTOR.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Replace your reproduction; guarantee fix in same session.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Describe symptom; let agent explore with Explore; read issue and execute plan with tdd.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. “Checkout doubles tax on discount.”
  2. Issue links for sprint.
  3. requirement-course-correction uses triage for bug class.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• aligned-implementation + tdd — execute.
  • triage-issue output matches tdd philosophy.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @triage-issue — Login redirect drops query string on mobile. Investigate and file gh issue with TDD plan.

docs.title: ubiquitous-language
docs.text: Skill package: ubiquitous-language/

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Builds a DDD-style glossary from the conversation, writes UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md in the working directory, and summarizes.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Domain discussion (nouns, verbs, workflows); optional existing file on re-run.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Markdown: grouped tables (term, definition, aliases to avoid), relationships, example dialogue, flagged ambiguities; inline summary + commitment to use terms.

docs.title: What it won’t do
docs.text: Include generic CS terms unless domain-specific; write long definitions.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Invoke after domain-heavy discussion; re-invoke to merge (new) / (updated) and refresh dialogue.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. E-commerce modeling session → glossary.
  2. “account” means Customer vs User — flagged.
  3. Share with team for PRD alignment.

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
• write-a-prd / prd-critique — consistent vocabulary.
  • grill-me — clarify terms before building.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: @ubiquitous-language — Extract glossary from our discussion of orders, fulfillments, shipments. Write UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.

docs.title: update-cursor-settings
